## What it is

Block clamped on the loaded end of the load cell. A vertical cylinder (radius 18, flat on the +X side at 109.5) on the tower axis, Z 10.7 to 18.7, with a 13 mm wide slot that takes the cell's last 23 mm. The tower stands on its flat top. It carries the two weak magnets of the lower joint, the M4 countersunk clamp screw, and the hex key hole of the stop screw, into which the tower's dowel drops. Printed upside down, top face on the bed: the part ends with `scale_flip`, the assembly flips it back. Bambu PETG Basic.

## Design notes

- Modelled in the machine frame and ends with `scale_frame` then `scale_flip`.
- Everything from `scale_layout()`. Slot: Z from the bottom to the cell's top, cell width plus 0.3 total, X from 0.2 mm west of the cell's tip through the flat. West of the tip the body stays solid and that end face locates the adapter along X. Upside down, the slot opens upward: no bridge.
- Top: flat, `adapter.top` = cell top + 3.0. The 3 mm is set by the magnet wells (2.2 deep, 0.8 of floor over the cell: `min_wall = 0.8`, 3 layers of 0.28); the head cone (2.43 with its recess) fits too.
- Clamp screw: M4 x 8 countersunk from above at the cell's inner hole, Ø4.5 clearance, 90° cone, head 0.2 under the top face, tip at Z 10.5: 5.2 mm into the cell. Upside down, the cone opens on the bed and narrows at 45°: the `bed_bevel` warning, accepted.
- Hex key hole: Ø5 (`adapter.key_hole`) over the stop screw at the cell's tip hole, through to the cell. The tower's dowel (Ø4.9) drops 1 mm into it. No chamfer on its rim (`dowel_hole_chamfer` 0): with the dowel 1 mm proud the tower tips off; the slider puts one back if a dowel ends up prouder.
- Weak magnets: two Ø5 x 2 wells open at the top face, 2.2 deep, so the magnet sits 0.2 below the surface. Each well ends in a 45° cone (`push_out_hole_cutter` in `system.py`) instead of a flat floor: upside down, the floor was a ring bridged over the well, and it printed as spaghetti that kept the magnet from going home. The 0.8 floor over the cell is shorter than the full taper (1.3 from Ø5.1 to Ø2.5), so the cone stops at the cell's top at Ø3.5 and the hole carries on at Ø3.5 to the bottom face, cutting a 1.5 mm groove into each side wall of the slot. With the adapter off the cell, a Ø2.5 pin gets the magnet out (they are in for good otherwise at +0.10). The magnet stops on the cone's rim, at the well's end.
- Checks accepted: four `floating` where the Ø3.5 circle crosses the slot's edges (the flank above is carried by the 45° cone; the rule trips on the cusp) and a `min_wall` of 0.31 on the cone's knife edge at the slot ceiling.
- Polish 1 mm: the vertical corners where the cylinder meets the flat, and the bottom rim. The top face's rim stays sharp: it is the bed face and the tower's seat.

## Don't

- Do not put the seat pyramid back: upright its overhangs did not slice, and the dowel plus the magnets place the tower (2026-11-17).
- Do not split it into a saddle and a screw adapter: considered on 2026-11-17, unnecessary once the top is flat.
- Do not thin the top under 3 mm over the cell: the magnet wells need 2.2 plus their floor.
- Do not chamfer the slot's edges or the top face: they mate with the cell and the tower.
- Do not close the slot's west end less than 0.2 mm from the cell's tip: the end face is the longitudinal locator.
- Do not give the magnet wells a flat floor back: printed upside down it is a ring bridged over the well, which turned to spaghetti and stopped the magnet short (2026-11-17).
- Do not move the wells or the key hole without the tower: its wells and dowel hole are over them by construction.
- Do not remove the final `scale_frame`: without it the part prints as its mirror image (found 2026-11-16: the PCB box came out on the wrong side of the cell).

## Changelog


- 2026-11-16 - First model: cylinder body with flat, cell slot, seat boss, clamp screw, stop screw access, two weak magnet wells.
- 2026-11-16 - Ends with `scale_frame` (Y reversed): the machine frame is left-handed, so the part was the mirror image of the real object.
- 2026-11-17 - 2 mm lower in the machine (bottom Z 12.7 -> 10.7), with the cell, after the base's floor went 4 -> 2 mm. The part itself is unchanged.
- 2026-11-17 - Magnet wells at the magnet's nominal diameter (`aimant_puit_press_fit` +0.15 -> 0.0): the +0.15 wells did not hold the magnets at all. On trial.
- 2026-11-17 - Magnet wells +0.10 over the magnet's diameter (`aimant_puit_press_fit` 0.0 -> 0.10): 0.0 was too tight. On trial.
- 2026-11-17 - Seat pyramid dropped: the top is flat, 3 mm over the cell instead of 2.5 + a 3 mm pyramid (top Z 21.2 -> 18.7), and the part prints upside down, so the slot needs no bridge (Bambu Studio refused the upright print). Stop screw hole Ø3 -> Ø4, which takes the tower's dowel. The M4 x 8 now goes 5.2 mm into the cell instead of 2.7.
- 2026-11-17 - 0.5 mm chamfer on the key hole's rim: printed, the tower only came off straight up.
- 2026-11-17 - Key hole chamfer back to 0 (a dowel pushed home, 1 mm proud, tips out without it). Ø1 push-out hole under each magnet.
- 2026-11-17 - Push-out holes Ø1 -> Ø1.5.
- 2026-11-17 - Push-out holes Ø2.5, for a 2.5 mm screwdriver; they cut a 1 mm groove into each side wall of the slot. Key hole Ø4 -> Ø5 for the dowel's 2.5 bore: 3.05 mm of plastic to the weak wells, 2.8 to the clamp screw's cone.
- 2026-11-17 - Magnet wells end in a 45° cone instead of a bridged floor (the floor printed as spaghetti and the magnets stayed proud of their recess); it stops at the cell's top at Ø3.5 and the push-out hole goes on at Ø3.5.
